---
title: "Accessing the data"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

Use the R functions for documented output tables, or read the published
canonical data — the versioned Parquet files distributed by `swelections` —
directly in other tools such as Python. The published files provide a stable
data basis for the corresponding release. Direct file access may require
selecting stored tables or combining files.
`swelections` is an R package; it does not provide separate Python,
Stata or SPSS packages.

## Source selection in R

The `source` argument controls how data are obtained. For most users, keep the
default `"auto"`; choose another source explicitly when you need a particular input:

- `"auto"` (default) selects approved canonical data for the requested election
  and function, otherwise a supported remote source. It never selects local raw
  files. If neither source is supported, the request gives an error.
- `"canonical"` explicitly reads the versioned Parquet files published in a
  swelections data release, without raw-source fallback.
- `"remote"` reads a current, official and explicitly supported Swedish Election
  Authority source, even when canonical data exist. It does not fall back to
  canonical or local data.
- `"local"` reads your own compatible saved raw archive, selected explicitly
  with `data_dir`.

Remote formats and coverage vary between elections and functions. A new
presentation file does not automatically replace a withdrawn detailed export.
See [Coverage](coverage.html) for availability and `data_sources` for detailed
source requirements. [Get started](swelections.html) shows the R interface.

## Saving source data locally

For supported remote raw-data sources, `source = "remote"` with
`update = TRUE` and `data_dir` saves the raw files needed by the call. Use the
same directory with `source = "local"` to repeat the request later without
downloading the source again:

```r
data_dir <- "my-data"

data_remote <- candidacies(
  year = 2026,
  election = "parliamentary",
  source = "remote",
  data_dir = data_dir,
  update = TRUE
)

data_local <- candidacies(
  year = 2026,
  election = "parliamentary",
  source = "local",
  data_dir = data_dir
)
```

Only the raw files needed by the call are saved. `archive = TRUE` is optional:
add it to the remote call to create a dated copy as well. It is not needed for
later local use. A dated copy can be replaced if the same source is fetched
again on the same day; use a separate directory for each snapshot you want
to preserve. `source = "local"` reads compatible raw source files, not a saved
output table. See the `data_sources` help page for source requirements.

To save an extracted output table instead, use `saveRDS(data_remote, "data.rds")`
and read it with `readRDS()`. Such a file is not an input archive for
`source = "local"`.

## Exporting tables

After retrieving a table in R, you can export it for use in other software.
CSV is a general import option. The separate R package `haven` can write Stata
`.dta` and SPSS `.sav` files:

```r
results_table <- results(year = 2022, election = "parliamentary", level = "national")
export_table <- results_table[, c("election_year", "party_code", "party_designation",
                                  "votes", "vote_share")]
write.csv(export_table, "results.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")

# Requires install.packages("haven")
haven::write_dta(export_table, "results.dta")
haven::write_sav(export_table, "results.sav")
```

The example selects a few columns for export. Stata variable names are limited
to 32 characters; some full swelections column names exceed that limit.

These are file exports, not separate swelections interfaces. Preserve identifiers
as text and check how the receiving program imports missing values. A CSV file
does not retain all R column types; do not replace missing values with zero.

## Published Parquet files

The [data-v0.4.1 release](https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/releases/tag/data-v0.4.1)
contains 200 Parquet files and 16 product manifests. A manifest identifies the
filenames, schema, sizes, SHA256 checksums and source provenance. Use the data
generation documented for your package version.

Some files contain several stored tables or geographic levels; other public
views require joins across files. Directly reading a file therefore need not
reproduce a complete `results()` call. Consult the manifest rather than combining
all rows or files indiscriminately.

## Reading a Parquet file in Python

Install `pandas` and a Parquet engine such as `pyarrow` in your Python environment.
This example reads published 2022 municipal election results directly. The
manifest is used for file verification: the byte count and SHA256 must match
before the data are read. The filter selects Stockholm municipality results,
keeping them separate from district and constituency rows. This is direct file access, not a Python API provided by `swelections`.

```python
import hashlib
import io
import json
from urllib.request import urlopen

import pandas as pd

base = "https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/releases/download/data-v0.4.1"
with urlopen(f"{base}/rkl2022-manifest.json") as response:
    manifest = json.load(response)

# This example targets the documented v0.4.1 storage contract.
assert manifest["schema_version"] == 3
asset = next(
    item for item in manifest["assets"]
    if item["file"] == "rkl2022-results-slutlig-kf.parquet"
)
with urlopen(f"{base}/{asset['file']}") as response:
    payload = response.read()

assert len(payload) == asset["bytes"]
assert hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() == asset["sha256"]

tables = pd.read_parquet(io.BytesIO(payload), engine="pyarrow")
stockholm = tables.loc[
    tables[".table"].eq("municipality")
    & tables["municipality_code"].eq("0180")
]
print(stockholm[["municipality_name", "party_abbreviation", "votes"]])
```

The file also contains district and municipal constituency rows. Its `.table` column distinguishes the
stored views; other files may use `.component` or additional selectors. Check
the manifest's `tables` entries and declared columns rather than assuming every
file has the same layout.

Retain the data-release identifier with your analysis. For technical category
and storage definitions, see the [value/storage contract](https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/blob/main/development/VALUE_CONTRACT.md).

## Other data resources

`swelections` is one way of accessing Swedish election data. Original sources
and related resources are also available from the organisations that produce,
preserve and distribute election statistics and research data.

### The Swedish Election Authority

The Swedish Election Authority publishes
[election results, statistics and raw data](https://www.val.se/valresultat-och-statistik/statistik-och-data)
in several formats. These official files underlie much of the material used
by `swelections`; the package does not replace the original source files.

### Complementary statistics from Statistics Sweden

Statistics Sweden (SCB) produces official election statistics. Its
[general-election statistics](https://www.scb.se/en/finding-statistics/statistics-by-subject-area/democracy/general-elections/general-elections-results/)
include links to aggregate tables in its PxWeb Statistical Database. These can
also be retrieved programmatically through the
[PxWeb API](https://www.scb.se/en/services/open-data-api/), for example with the
R package [pxweb](https://ropengov.github.io/pxweb/). This is a complementary
resource, not a swelections interface.

Statistics Sweden also publishes statistics on
[nominated and elected candidates](https://www.scb.se/en/finding-statistics/statistics-by-subject-area/democracy/general-elections/general-elections-nominated-and-elected-candidates/),
[elected representatives and their assignments](https://www.scb.se/en/finding-statistics/statistics-by-subject-area/democracy/general-statistics/survey-of-elected-representatives-in-municipalities-and-county-councils/)
and [electoral participation](https://www.scb.se/en/finding-statistics/statistics-by-subject-area/democracy/general-elections/general-elections-participation-survey/),
with breakdowns by background characteristics. More detailed microdata are not
open data or part of `swelections`. Research access may be possible after
disclosure and eligibility assessment; the
[English guidance](https://www.scb.se/en/services/ordering-data-and-statistics/microdata/)
states that release requires a Swedish entity responsible for research. Check
the conditions and available variables for the specific project; see also the
[microdata FAQ](https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/mikrodata/fragor-och-svar/).

### Swedish National Data Service (SND)

[SND](https://snd.se/en) makes research data discoverable and accessible through
[Researchdata.se](https://researchdata.se/en), including historical Swedish
electoral datasets and other election-related research data. Some historical
datasets, such as [Swedish electoral data for the 2002 general election](https://researchdata.se/en/catalogue/dataset/snd0237-10),
use Statistics Sweden data processed and documented for research. Other
election-related collections have different producers and sources; check each
dataset's documentation and access conditions.

These resources can be useful for original source files, alternative formats,
statistics outside swelections coverage and related election research data.
